title: The 10 Best Mini Chainsaws
subtitle: Cordless 6 and 8-inch mini chainsaws for pruning and small limbs, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A mini chainsaw is a light, one-handed battery saw for pruning and small branches, and one of Amazon's best-selling gift tools. We ranked 10 best-sellers from SEESII, Tietoc, Greenworks, CRAFTSMAN, DEWALT and others on rating, review volume and features (two batteries, auto oiling, a brushless motor and an 8-inch bar option).
data_source: Amazon product listings on the data_captured date. Prices, ratings and review counts change daily; check the listing before relying on a number.

avoid.name: Mini Chainsaw Cordless, 6 Inch Electric Chainsaw with 2000MAH Battery, 1000W
avoid.flag: 1,000 W and 30 minutes from a 21V 2Ah battery
avoid.verdict: Its power and runtime claims can't both be true on the battery it ships with.
reasons: A 21V 2,000 mAh battery holds about 42 watt-hours. Running a 1,000 W motor for the claimed 'up to 30 minutes of continuous operation' would take about 500 watt-hours, roughly 12 times what the battery holds.
With the headline numbers inflated, nothing else in the listing can be compared to the SEESII and Tietoc saws, which have thousands of reviews.
It has 85 reviews; the Tietoc MNCS-118 costs the same, has an auto oiler and 19,340 reviews.

buyers_guide.q: What's a mini chainsaw good for?
buyers_guide.a: Pruning shrubs and small trees, cutting branches up to about 4 to 6 inches, and storm cleanup of small limbs. They're not for felling trees or cutting firewood logs.
6-inch saws are lighter and easier one-handed. 8-inch bars cut thicker limbs. Kits with both bars give you the choice.
Treat them as marketing. A 21V 2Ah battery holds about 42 watt-hours, so a mini saw can't run at 1,000 W for long. Look at cut counts, battery size and reviews instead.

buyers_guide.q: Do I need to oil it?
buyers_guide.a: Yes. Auto-oilers feed bar oil while you cut; others need oil added by hand. Running a dry chain ruins it quickly.
They're easier to control than a full saw, but they still cut flesh. Use both hands when you can, wear gloves and eye protection, and keep the guard on.
